edit.prompt: You are given TWO images. The FIRST image is a CONTROL MAP: solid GREEN regions are LAND, solid BLUE regions are SEA water. Redraw the FIRST image in the EXACT art style, muted sepia colour palette, fine cross-hatched linework and weathered antique look of the SECOND image. CRITICAL: the LAND and SEA SHAPES — island positions, sizes and coastlines — come ENTIRELY from the FIRST control image. Put antique inked LAND in every GREEN region and SEA in every BLUE region, keeping the same islands and landmasses in the SAME positions, sizes and overall shapes as the control. Do NOT copy the islands, coastlines, continents or overall composition of the SECOND image — it is ONLY a style reference, not a map to reproduce. Draw a NATURAL hand-drawn COASTLINE where land meets water: a soft, irregular, gently wandering shore with a thin lighter beach and shallow-water shading that eases the land into the sea — NEVER a hard mechanical outline and never a straight or geometric edge; sparser and lighter texture near the shore, dense and dark inland. Draw ONLY natural terrain — cross-hatched mountains, ridges, forests, hills, grassland and the scalloped seigaiha wave sea. Do NOT draw any castles, keeps, forts, towers, watchtowers, houses, villages, buildings or man-made structures anywhere — those are added separately later. This is a flat overhead map that fills the ENTIRE frame edge to edge — no horizon, no sky, no perspective, no empty margin, no labels, no text, no border. CRITICAL MAPPING: green control region becomes antique inked LAND, blue control region becomes the scalloped seigaiha wave SEA. Do not swap them.
